evals.prompt: Run these five questions against our Fini bot, stage one guideline change to fix the failures, let me review it, then publish and retest.
evals.expected_output: An active baseline, classification, minimal full-array prompt draft, exact-ID draft validation, exact publish, re-fetch, and marked active retest workflow.
assertions: Fetches the complete current prompt before editing
Classifies failures before deciding the prompt is responsible
Preserves all three prompt arrays in the draft
Fetches and reviews the exact draft version ID
Requires a complete non-truncated exact-version payload before publication
Routes baseline-versus-draft behavior proof through fini-api-draft-validation with markAsTest true
Passes only the persisted promptVersionId and keeps baseline/candidate cases like-for-like
Publishes only the exact reviewed version
Re-fetches active prompts and reruns the same questions

evals.prompt: Create an escalation rule from these instructions, but do not make it live yet.
evals.expected_output: Uses a rule draft, inspects the resulting flow, and leaves bot assignment and publishing for later approval.
assertions: Generates and inspects a preview, then persists it as an intent DRAFT
Does not assume draft botIds imply live assignment
Reports the persisted rule ID and draft version ID
Reports the review and publish steps still required

evals.prompt: Import these Zendesk articles into our knowledge base.
evals.expected_output: Routes to sources and knowledge workflows rather than treating ingestion as agent prompt configuration.
assertions: Does not use prompt, rule, or tag updates for a source-ingestion request
Routes to fini-api-sources and fini-api-knowledge

evals.prompt: Refine this escalation rule, then publish the version I just approved to one bot.
evals.expected_output: Refines the same intent rule as a draft version, avoids an orphan duplicate, and publishes the exact reviewed draftVersionId after confirmation.
assertions: Reads the full rule and field context before changing the flow
Updates the same intent rule as DRAFT instead of duplicating it
Identifies the exact reviewed draftVersionId
Requires explicit target botIds and publish approval
Passes the explicitly reviewed draftVersionId and never resolves a current or latest draft implicitly

evals.prompt: Publish prompt draft pv_older now. Someone else may have updated this agent since I drafted it.
evals.expected_output: Fetches the exact stale draft, its exact parent, and the exact latest active lifecycle version, then performs a conflict-aware three-way rebase into a newly reviewable draft instead of retrying the old version.
assertions: Fetches the exact stale draft, its exact parent, and the exact latest active lifecycle version before publication
Uses parentVersionId or the stale publish response to identify staleness
Does not retry or force-publish the stale version ID
Fetches the exact parent lifecycle version and derives draft-versus-parent changes
Detects conflicts between the exact parent and exact latest active prompt before creating a new draft
Requires review of the replacement draft ID before publishing it

evals.prompt: This is an emergency and I explicitly want these complete prompt arrays live immediately, without a draft review step.
evals.expected_output: Uses the documented direct Update prompts alternative, verifies the new saved version, and does not misdescribe it as an in-place patch.
assertions: Recognizes the caller explicitly chose the direct-live path
Uses complete planning, guideline, and channel arrays
Uses the documented public prompt update route
Re-fetches current prompts and history after the write
Explains that direct update still saves a new version

evals.prompt: We created a Cancel Subscription Action. Assign it to our support agent so it runs when customers ask to cancel.
evals.expected_output: Wires the exact Action ID into a Rulebook Tool node under the cancellation flow and publishes the reviewed rule to the support agent; it does not rely on Action assignment junctions.
assertions: Fetches the Action input and output contract
Adds a Tool node that references the exact Action ID
Binds required inputs and downstream outputs
Uses the rule's bot assignment to control agent reachability
States that Action assignment junctions are not runtime gates

evals.prompt: Evaluate our refund Rulebook with a sample conversation and tell me which path it takes.
evals.expected_output: Inspects required test fields and the full rule before evaluation, identifies Tool nodes, uses controlled input context, and reports node results plus any external effects.
assertions: Fetches the rule test fields before building input context
Inspects the flow for Action Tool nodes
Does not call the evaluation read-only when an Action can run
Uses explicit controlled test inputs
Reports path, node results, Action calls, and remaining regression coverage

evals.prompt: We just created a brand-new unassigned cancellation Rulebook draft. Run that exact draft against the bot before publishing it.
evals.expected_output: Explains that a brand-new unassigned rule draft is not available to the bot for a ruleVersionIds runtime override; previews its fields and flow structurally, then offers a supported review/publish path without pretending it executed.
assertions: Does not claim Generate Answer can execute a brand-new unassigned rule draft
Uses Preview rule test fields only for structural input discovery
Does not call the published-rule evaluation route for the draft
Explains that a draft override is supported only when the owning rule is already published and assigned to the target bot
Keeps any Action Tool-node side effects explicit for a later supported execution

evals.prompt: Delete custom tag group 55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555555. I confirm that exact group is obsolete.
evals.expected_output: Uses the existing exact-target authorization, verifies the group is workspace-owned, inventories its tags and Rulebook/reporting dependencies, deletes only that group, and re-lists to verify absence.
assertions: Lists and resolves the exact tag group before deletion
Verifies it is workspace-owned rather than a Fini-managed default
Inventories contained tags plus Rulebook and reporting dependencies
Does not ask for duplicate confirmation
Deletes only the exact supplied tag group ID
Re-lists groups and reports the absence check and remaining dependency risk

evals.prompt: Duplicate rule rule_refunds so I can experiment with the copy.
evals.expected_output: Fetches the exact source and its actual kind, explains that the independent copy can be live or assigned, and waits for exact-source confirmation before duplicating and re-fetching the copy.
assertions: Fetches rule_refunds and uses the returned type rather than a caller-supplied or default type
Treats duplication as live-impacting for both intent and Business Rules
Explains that the copy may be published or assigned and does not promise a harmless draft
Requires exact confirmation bound to rule_refunds before calling Duplicate rule
Re-fetches the returned copy and reports its actual ID, state, kind, assignments, and Action reachability

evals.prompt: Publish the current escalation rule draft to bot_support. I do not have the draft version ID.
evals.expected_output: Does not auto-resolve a current or latest draft after approval; lists versions, fetches one exact complete candidate for review, and requires approval bound to its explicit draftVersionId before publishing.
assertions: Refuses to call Publish rule draft without an explicit draftVersionId
Lists versions and fetches the exact candidate rather than silently selecting current or latest
Requires complete review of the candidate version
Binds publish approval to that exact draftVersionId and explicit bot_support target
Does not substitute a rule ID, version number, or inferred latest draft for draftVersionId

evals.prompt: Refine Business Rule rule_vip as a draft and publish it after review.
evals.expected_output: Fetches the exact rule, identifies it as a Business Rule, refuses the cross-kind draft/refine/publish workflow, and explains that any update is immediate-live and needs an exact reviewed diff plus live-write confirmation.
assertions: Fetches rule_vip and verifies its actual returned kind before choosing a lifecycle
Does not call intent refine, version-history, restore, or publish routes for a Business Rule
Explains that Business Rules are immediate-live and non-versioned
Does not coerce the rule by passing type intent or status DRAFT
Offers a full re-fetch, exact diff review, confirmation, immediate update, and post-write verification path

evals.prompt: Get the Rulebook draft whose version ID is rv_escalation. I passed rv_escalation to Get rule and it returned 404.
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes the stable parent ruleId from rv_escalation's versionId, explains why Get rule can 404, resolves the parent, then fetches the exact version using both identifiers.
assertions: Does not pass rv_escalation to Get rule as though it were the parent ruleId
Explains that Get rule requires the parent ruleId while versionStatus is optional and only selects DRAFT or PUBLISHED
Resolves or requests the parent ruleId before fetching the exact version
Uses both the parent ruleId and rv_escalation with Get rule version
Does not claim the 404 proves the rule version was deleted

evals.prompt: List our Reply Rules and explain the conditions that choose no reply, internal comment, or direct reply. Do not change anything.
evals.expected_output: Reads all three workspace Reply Rule slots and fields context, then explains the current conditions without treating them as Rulebooks or mutating configuration.
assertions: Uses both Get Reply Rules and Get Reply Rule fields context
Reports noReply, internalComment, and directReply independently
Uses returned fields context to interpret paths, operators, quantifiers, Attributes, tags, and sources
Treats an empty disabled slot as unconfigured rather than missing
Does not request or invent a bot ID or workspace ID
Does not substitute Rulebook list, test, evaluation, draft, or publish operations
Makes no mutation claim
